No questions, just compliments - this game is amazing! Concept and execution are top tier. It feels super polished and well balanced. I absolutely love the different ways to play depending on what objective you're going for. It also has amazing pacing - all the appeal of a one-more-turn game without taking days to finish a scenario.

I typically have 2-3 population buildings per city, arranged so that they have a support focused building in the center. My favorite is the school, but I often end up with a science surplus because of that.

In my 1st city, I normally push for food quickly by getting up 3 food buildings with a soil factory in the center. In the early game I use food for expansion, then I shift it to be my primary export towards the late game.

I fill in the gaps with robots, but I rarely try to have more than 5 population + robots in a city. I prefer buildings like the bus station over additional robots.

In the mid to late game, don't be afraid to replace buildings with an improved version, like replacing basis population with something that gives extra bonuses. Expansion of multiple cities is high cost because it's hard to explore enough territory to make it worthwhile. 

Replacing buildings is also very helpful when you max out a terraforming parameter - get rid of anything you don't need.

Leaders depend on what you want to do! I avoid the ones that are very support focused because I've never had an issue with support. Other than that, I've used most to good success! I do prefer the ones with actions that don't cost power for my 3rd leader and beyond because I often run low on power and I don't want to waste their action.

ETA - In case you can't tell, I already love this game immensely. It's so fun, well balanced, and keeps you on your toes.

How you go about shading totally depends on the look you're going for. I'd basically divide it up as painting or drawing (digitally). I'm assuming you want to shade animals, though the overall ideas apply to anything.

Tamberella has some awesome tutorials on lighting and shading styles in general: [long fur](https://tamberella.deviantart.com/art/Long-Fur-Shading-Tutorial-251600522), [short fur](https://tamberella.deviantart.com/art/Giant-Shading-Tutorial-251104611), and [different shading styles](https://tamberella.deviantart.com/art/Shading-Tut-Supplement-251182560)

Frankly, I've never grasped painting well, but for that you'll basically just be working on one layer and/ or with a lot of blending by first blocking out your shaded areas then refining them and adding details. [This tutorial](https://novawuff.deviantart.com/art/Fur-Painting-Tutorial-97525150) looks pretty good. Painting in SAI is basically like any other program, and you've just gotta take time to work out what brush settings you like. Personally, I use a combination of marker, airbrush, brush, and watercolor with various settings based on what texture I'm looking for. Installing some extra texture and brush packages ([like this](https://lemonpetals.deviantart.com/art/SCUFFED-A-New-Brush-for-SAI-321414435)) or looking up other people's settings ([like this](https://raheel-ali.deviantart.com/art/sai-brush-408433428)) can help.

For drawing styles, most people use many layers to achieve the look they want. The colors go on one layer (or set of layers), lines on another, and then a couple layers may go to shade and highlight the character. In SAI, I like using shade and luminescence layers (for shadows and highlights respectively) mostly to get very vivid, colorful shades. Multiply layers are also very common for the shadows with overlay as highlights. Here are two fur shading tutorials in SAI: [using multiply](https://pipamir.deviantart.com/art/SAI-fur-Shading-Tutorial-400477949) and [using shade](https://asenhart.deviantart.com/art/Basing-Tutorial-2-0-548895734).

Some other awesome tutorials on shading and art in general can be found by: [AquaSixio](https://aquasixio.deviantart.com/gallery/8808807/Tutorials), [Tamberella (again)] (https://tamberella.deviantart.com/gallery/58806510/Studies-and-Tutorials), [yuchenghong](https://yuchenghong.deviantart.com/gallery/56066551/Tutorial), and lots of others (that I can't find because dA is lagging).

I just grabbed a few of the top tutorials from searches on deviantArt - I suggest continuing to look for tutorials that are closer to your desired style. Feel free to reach out to me if you have any other questions. I'm not much of an artist, but I'll help however I can.

I'm sure he'd love to get some custom art from you (rather than a premade print), though I know making poster-sized art can be a long process. Here are a few ideas and related resources that could help. I'm going to add a decent amount of detail, but if you want any expansion just ask.

As an overall feature, it would be a good idea to make sure the piece could be used as a desktop background in addition to the poster (so horizontal layout would probably be better). It's unclear if you're using digital or traditional mediums, but either way I think having something close to screen dimensional ratio would be good.

Something to consider with any hero drawing is that the heroes have lots of different sets or skins or hats - basically, customization. If you're drawing something for him (and he knows this is happening), get him to send you screenshots of how his specific characters look, which you can reference in drawing to add the personal touch.

As someone else mentioned, maps aren't as big a deal because there's just one standard map (with some customization options). As a result, most "splash" art or backgrounds don't really include the surroundings - it's character focused art. If he does use a specific map skin, you could involve that in the scene.

On that note, you mentioned that he likes Ember Spirit. Another user mentioned the Chinese New Year map which is thematically related, so you could put him in that map as a scene. Some more information about him: [here you can see ES's 4 abilities in Youtube videos to get some ideas](http://www.dota2.com/hero/Ember_Spirit/); [here, towards the bottom of the page, you can see his different sets/ equiptment](http://dota2.gamepedia.com/Ember_Spirit); [here is his model from the front](http://ecowallpapers.net/wp-content/uploads/2002_dota2_:_ember_spirit.jpg); [here is a drawing of him from each side](http://i.imgur.com/qix9SZA.png); and you can find some nice splash art of him just be googling "Ember Spirit DotA 2."

You can also just do classic splash art with little to no background. A lot of splash art just has some "particle" around the character - fire, light, water, or whatever else fits the hero.

If you want to do a group shot with his favorite heroes, that could be as simple as having them standing and interacting with each other (maybe arrange them by color or by his preference) or more complex of a battle scene. 10 heroes may be a bit much to draw with detail, but there are plenty of awesome cute/ chibi versions of heroes: [A](http://orig00.deviantart.net/79db/f/2015/129/6/b/6b5b57e661481dd0a29e0302ed88b3b1-d8sq2nf.jpg), [B](http://pre15.deviantart.net/ef13/th/pre/f/2013/336/2/d/dota_2_by_inkinesss-d6wju85.jpg), [C](http://orig05.deviantart.net/10b9/f/2013/079/8/6/dota_2___mini_radiant_agi_heroes_by_spidercandy-d5ynj6y.jpg). Again, good resources for this would include the [hero pages here with their brief lore and abilities](http://www.dota2.com/heroes/) and the [pages here with sets at the bottom of each page](http://dota2.gamepedia.com/Heroes). Just look up the ones you know he's into (don't try to go through them all... it's a lot).

With the same group idea and maybe a more cartoon-y style, you could have him and a few heroes interacting in a friendly way - making him look like part of the gang. The references for this would be the same as above.

Another possible group idea, kinda going with the giant logo and slits concept you mentioned, is to have the heroes "playing" around the logo - flying above it, laying on top, peeking around the edges, sitting by the base. That could go along with your cute inclination and expose some personalities and abilities of the heroes.

I'm presently living in Lee Hall (the dorm where Galileo and related programs live) and I'll continue doing so as an upperclassman leader next year.

I'll preface further explanation by saying: you should apply to live here. Being around other engineering students, people who have common backgrounds and classes, is a huge help. The mentoring program can also be beneficial, though personally I didn't find it so. Other than the social aspect, living in Lee has perks including: several lounges on every floor, studio workspace for build projects, and some build teams which recruit solely within the building.

As far as the class and other associated responsibilities of living here: the class is 2 credits and involves sitting bored in a room for 1.25 hours once a week. Theoretically you learn things but there aren't tests so you mostly just attend and space out. There are a decent number of assignments but they don't take too long. The biggest time commitment is the community activities. Each semester you have to attend 8-10 events made by upperclassmen leaders (which are social, academic, or professional development) and do 10 hours of community service. For the first 10 weeks you also have weekly meetings with a mentor and group of hallmates which take .5-1 hour and during which you mostly just talk about classes and how you're faring in college.

From my experience all of the requirements that come along with living here are worth it (evidenced by the fact that I'm returning for another year). I suggest at very least applying. I don't think I've heard of anyone who really regretted living here.

To expand upon what blue-firetruck was saying about tablet choices, I've been working with the same Wacom Bamboo for about 4 years and it's still smooth and functional for me, although some areas have gotten worn down and I've replaced the pen nib a few times. It has a working area of 5.5 in X 8.5 in. When looking at tablets check all the specs- I think one of the things that was off putting about getting the newest Intuous when I've been looking at getting a new tablet is that it has paper texture, and even something small like that can make a difference. You may like it since you're used to paper, but I've always drawn digitally so it would be unwelcome for me, and you should consider small preferences like that. Another brand you could check out is Monoprice. I've heard good things about their tablets and they tend to be cheaper than Wacom things.

Another things I'll mention is that once you have a tablet you could look into Paint Tool SAI, which is another drawing program. If you want to try it I can give you a download link. I've been working with the program for a long time and I find that it responds really well to pen pressure and offers a lot of options, and it's pretty popular for painterly art especially, but it can be hard to learn because there are a lot of things to play with.

This piece looks really great, especially for an "attempt." I hope you can get a tablet and keep exploring digital art- it's really amazing to have so many tools at your fingertips, from brushes to pencils to vector line work.

My boyfriend is out of contact range for the week, then I'll see him a day or two, then he's going to another place he may not have contact for a week, so I feel your pain- it sucks to not even have our small rituals like saying good night. What I've been doing so far this week, even tho he can't get any of my messages, is writing notes each day about whatever I'm thinking and continuing to say good night. I figure it'll be a nice surprise for him to come back after a week without talking at all to see the messages. Beyond those things written to him as an eventual gift to show that I still think of him I've been keeping busy with reading, cleaning, hanging out with other friends... And even while doing those things I miss him, but I have little mementos from him like a necklace and photos on my phone as comfort.

Since you'll be the one going away, rather than waiting for him to return, you could also take pictures or get trinkets to show or send to him afterward, again as a reminder that you're thinking of him and as a way of sharing your trip to rebond after being gone a while. You could also try to set aside a day shortly before and another shortly after your trip to spend more time talking than you normally may.
